description: The LCS problem has a natural tropical (max-plus) algebraic formulation: the DP recurrence is a max-plus matrix product. Tropical geometry studies the combinatorial structure of solutions to such optimization problems. By analyzing the tropical variety of the LCS problem, one may extract structural constraints that tighten bounds.
mathematical_formalization: The LCS DP table L(i,j) = max(L(i-1,j), L(i,j-1), L(i-1,j-1) + 1[x_i = y_j]) is a tropical polynomial. The anti-diagonal evolution is a max-plus matrix-vector product. The Lyapunov exponent of the random product of max-plus transition matrices equals gamma_2.
analogical_connections: Max-plus linear algebra and shortest path problems
implementation_hypothesis: Compute the max-plus transition matrices for binary LCS. Analyze the tropical eigenvalue (Lyapunov exponent) of the random product. Use Oseledec's theorem to bound the convergence rate.
experiment_seed: For n=1..30, compute exact distribution of max-plus matrix products. Extract Lyapunov exponent. Compare with E[lambda_{n,2}]/n.
